chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Duras ibn A'yan who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about two men in the state of Ihram who threw (a dart or stone) at game, and one of them hit it. He said: 'On each of them is the redemption (kaffarah).'
If a Muhrim (one in Ihram) and a Muhill (one not in Ihram) kill game, then on the Muhrim is the full redemption, and on the Muhill is half the redemption. He narrated.

key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One not in the state of Ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمَيْنِ: Two men in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on redemption for two people hunting together while one or both are in Ihram?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the liability of *fidyah* (redemption) when two individuals hunt while in *Ihram*, establishing that both bear the full penalty, whereas a mixed pair results in the *Muhrim* paying fully and the *Muḥill* paying half. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the state of *Ihram* is the primary determinant for the full obligation, while the non-pilgrim shares in the act but bears reduced liability. The narration underscores the precision in distinguishing between joint action and individual status in ritual law.
